units: <cite ref="Mishnah Oktzin 3:4">Ukts. III, 4</cite> <he>עד שיִמְתּוֹקוּ</he> until they are made palatable (by pressing).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 85:3">Gen. R. s. 85</cite> <he>יִמְתַּק לכם</he> may it be sweet to (well agree with) you, v. <cite ref="B01003"><he>בָּסַם</he></cite>.
Yalk. Job 910 (ref. to Job XXIV, 20) שמָתַק רמה מהם the worm gnawed at them with delight; Gen. R. s. 33 שמִיתְּקוּ רמה מהם (Pi.) the worms did &c.—

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 962:15">Yalk. Prov. 962</cite> <he>סופו להיות מוֹתֵק עליו</he> shall finally feed on him; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 961:29">ib. 961</cite> <he>מותח</he> (corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Tosefta Beitsah 3:15">Tosef. Bets. III, 15</cite> <he>אין מְמַתְּקִין וכ׳</he> you must not (on the Holy Day) sweeten a mustard mixture by dipping a live coal into it; <cite ref="Shabbat 134a">Sabb. 134ᵃ</cite>; Y. Bets. IV, 62ᶜ bot.
<cite ref="Shabbat 90a:1">Sabb. 90ᵃ</cite> <he>למַתֵּק קדרה</he> to season a dish.

Ber. 5ᵃ מלח מְמַתֶּקֶת וכ׳ salt seasons the meat; a. fr.—Trnsf. to pacify. Y. Ab. Zar. II, 42ᵃ top והוא יודע למתק וכ׳ he knows how to calm the great Ocean. Y. Meg. III, 74ᵃ bot. (in a secret letter) תמר … ובקשנו למַתְּקָה וכ׳ Tamar still endures in her bitterness (hostility), and we attempted to sweeten her (by bribery), ‘but the melter has refined in vain’ (Jer. VI, 29).

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 961:29">Yalk. Prov. 961</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 29:21">Prov. XXIX, 21</cite>) <he>כל מי שמְמַתֵּק וכ׳</he> he who indulges his passion in his youth (v. <cite ref="M01746"><he>מָנוֹן</he></cite>).—

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:16">Cant. R. to V, 16</cite> (play on <cite ref="M01691"><he>ממתקים</he></cite>, <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:16">ib.</cite>) <he>ה׳ להם וכ׳</he> he sweetened (softened) the word for them; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 10">Num. R. s. 10</cite>, beg.

senses.gloss: to become sweet, to be quieted. Y. Ab. Zar. l. c. בשעה שהמים … מִתְמַתְּקִין when the waters praise their Creator, they grow calm.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 13">Gen. R. s. 13</cite>, a. e. <he>מִתְמַתְּקִים הן בעבים</he> (some ed. <he>ממת׳</he>, corr. acc.) the salt water becomes sweet in the clouds; <cite ref="Taanit 9b">Taan. 9ᵇ</cite> Ms. M. (ed. <cite ref="M01691"><he>ממתקין</he></cite>, corr. acc.).
